title: Tides, Tears & the Spice Must Flow
description: A game for curious adults: deep ocean science, Dune lore, Renaissance-era authors, fan fiction culture, YouTube royalty, and movies guaranteed to wreck you.

questions.question: The largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth, this marine mammal can grow to 100 feet long and produces calls louder than a jet engine.
Built by tiny coral polyps over centuries, this calcium carbonate structure is called the 'rainforest of the sea' due to the staggering diversity it supports.
This Pacific fish famously leaves the open ocean to return to the exact freshwater stream where it was born, spawning once before dying.
The deepest known point on Earth, located in the western Pacific's Mariana Trench, plunges nearly 36,000 feet below sea level and bears this name.
Sharks and rays use these jelly-filled sensory pores to detect the electrical fields of camouflaged prey, named for the Italian anatomist who first described them in the 1500s.
questions.answer: What are the ampullae of Lorenzini?

questions.question: Known as 'the spice,' this substance found only on Arrakis is the most valuable commodity in the universe, granting extended life and enabling interstellar navigation.
Paul Atreides belongs to this noble house, which accepts stewardship of Arrakis at the opening of Herbert's novel — only to be betrayed almost immediately.
These desert-dwelling people of Arrakis walk with a stilted, arrhythmic gait to avoid attracting the giant sandworms that hunt by sensing rhythmic vibrations in the sand.
Paul's mother Lady Jessica belongs to this ancient sisterhood that uses selective breeding and mental conditioning in a millennia-long program to cultivate a superhuman messiah.
The Fremen word 'Lisan al-Gaib' means off-world prophet; the private Fremen name Paul takes for himself — meaning 'the desert mouse that cannot be caught' — is this.
While imprisoned in Spain, this author began writing about a deluded knight who charges at windmills, producing what many scholars call the world's first modern novel.
This Florentine diplomat wrote The Prince, advising rulers that it is better to be feared than loved and that the ends justify the means in political life.
This English humanist coined the word 'utopia' in a 1516 Latin work and was beheaded by Henry VIII after refusing to endorse the king's break from Rome.
A contemporary of Shakespeare, this English playwright wrote Doctor Faustus and Tamburlaine before dying at age 29 in a Deptford tavern under mysterious circumstances.
This French writer invented the personal essay in his 1580 Essais, capturing his restless curiosity with the guiding motto 'Que sçay-je?' — 'What do I know?'
Originally written as Twilight fan fiction under the title 'Master of the Universe,' this bestselling series was published after the author swapped in new character names.
questions.answer: What is Fifty Shades of Grey?

questions.question: Abbreviated 'AU,' this fan fiction subgenre reimagines familiar characters in a completely different setting or timeline, such as Harry Potter being sorted into Slytherin.
This fan-run archive, launched in 2009 after frustrations with FanFiction.net's content policies, won a Hugo Award for Best Related Work in 2019.
questions.answer: What is Archive of Our Own?

questions.question: The term 'slash fiction,' referring to romantic fan stories pairing same-sex characters, originated from the 1970s fan community surrounding this iconic sci-fi duo.
Held twice yearly in Tokyo, this massive doujinshi event is the world's largest gathering for unofficial fan-created works based on anime, manga, and games.
Known for extravagant philanthropy stunts and record-breaking subscriber counts, this creator born Jimmy Donaldson was the first individual to reach 200 million YouTube subscribers.
Known by the initials MKBHD, this tech reviewer from New Jersey has built one of YouTube's most respected gadget channels, known for meticulous and visually stunning product breakdowns.
This YouTube educator built a massive science following by asking impossibly large questions, like 'What is the biggest number?' and exploring the nature of human perception and reality.
This former NASA engineer turned YouTube creator rose to fame building elaborate contraptions and rigorously testing viral science claims, amassing tens of millions of subscribers.
This North Carolina duo, childhood friends since elementary school, have hosted 'Good Mythical Morning' on YouTube every weekday since 2012 as the platform's most consistent daily creators.
This 2009 Pixar film opens with a wordless four-minute montage showing a couple's entire life together — including a heartbreaking loss — before the main story even begins.
In this 1982 Spielberg film, a lonely boy befriends a stranded alien, and audiences worldwide were left in tears when the creature boards his ship and says goodbye.
In this 2010 Pixar sequel, a group of toys hold hands and silently face a furnace, accepting their apparent fate in one of animation's most emotionally crushing sequences.
In this 1991 film, a girl's best friend — severely allergic to bees — runs into the woods searching for her lost mood ring and never comes back.
This 1988 Studio Ghibli film, set in wartime Japan, follows a teenage boy's agonizing effort to keep his young sister alive amid starvation and firebombing.
questions.answer: What is Grave of the Fireflies?
